vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clipboard-memory
Version: 1.3.0

The clipboard-memory skill enables an AI agent to search and retrieve macOS clipboard history using the clipmem CLI tool. It includes a diagnostic shell script (scripts/check-setup.sh) and extensive documentation (references/). While the functionality is aligned with the stated purpose of clipboard recovery, the skill is classified as suspicious because it provides programmatic access to highly sensitive information (e.g., passwords or keys previously copied by the user) and utilizes shell execution for its core operations. No evidence of intentional malice, data exfiltration, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill is internally coherent: it only needs a macOS-only CLI (clipmem), its instructions call that CLI and local checks, and the requested install/paths match the described clipboard-recall purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description describe a macOS clipboard archive reader and the skill only requires the clipmem binary and access to the clipmem SQLite archive under ~/Library/Application Support/clipmem/ — these are appropriate and expected for the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and provided scripts instruct the agent to run only local clipmem commands and a local health-check script; they reference the local DB path and the watcher service (expected). Minor note: scripts call python3 for JSON parsing but python3 is not declared as a required binary in registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install is via Homebrew (formula: tristanmanchester/tap/clipmem) which is a plausible delivery method. Metadata also references a cargo install alternative in the docs. This is reasonable but worth verifying the tap/package origin before installing (third-party tap).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials and only needs local file access to the clipmem DB — this is proportionate to a clipboard-recall skill. Reminder: clipboard contents often include sensitive secrets, so the data the skill can surface is itself highly sensitive.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and standard agent invocation are set. The skill does not request permanent elevated privileges or modify other skills' configs. Its expected on-disk footprint (skill files, health-check script) is normal.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: run the local 'clipmem' CLI and read the local clipboard archive. Before installing, verify the clipmem package source (the Homebrew tap referenced is a third-party tap), and only install from a source you trust. Be aware the skill will surface anything you've copied (URLs, commands, file paths, images, PDFs, and potentially secrets like passwords or API keys) because that's the point — treat outputs as sensitive. Also note the included health-check script invokes python3 (not declared as a required binary); ensure your environment/sandbox provides python3 and that the OpenClaw agent has permission to run the binary and read ~/Library/Application Support/clipmem/clipmem.sqlite3. If you have concerns about exposing clipboard contents remotely, restrict or avoid installing: even though the skill itself is local, results returned by an agent can be transmitted by the platform or logged elsewhere.
